evals.prompt: add liveness and readiness probes to this deployment
evals.expected_output: Adds a startup probe to protect slow boots, a liveness probe that only fails on genuinely unrecoverable states, and a readiness probe that fails whenever the pod cannot currently serve traffic without restarting it, explaining why each threshold was chosen.

Directs the user to kubectl describe pod and events before logs, checks kubectl logs --previous and the exit code (137 is SIGKILL/OOM, 1 is an application error), and states the exact Event line that explains the state rather than guessing.

evals.prompt: just set memory limit way higher than requests so it never gets OOMKilled
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: limits should be backed by observed usage, not guessed, and a wide limit-vs-request gap undermines QoS class and overcommit accuracy; recommends profiling actual usage and considering requests == limits for Guaranteed QoS where eviction order matters.
